[h2]Verdict[/h2]

Not the best Call of Duty, but definitely one of the better ones for me.

[h2]My history with the game[/h2]
I finished Call of Duty: Ghosts in 5.7 hours (on Veteran difficulty).

This was my second full playthrough. I first played it sometime around 2018, but I actually wanted to play it much earlier, around its original release in 2013.

Back then, I still had an older PC build from 2007, and Ghosts was one of the first Call of Duty games where the system requirements felt noticeably higher. I remember installing it, trying to launch it, and the game simply refused to start because of an error.

I think this was probably one of the reasons why Ghosts had a rougher reception and why Activision never made Ghosts 2.

[h2]Quick signals[/h2]
💸 Value: ✅ Worth playing at least once
🖥️ Requirements: ✅ Easy to run today, but demanding back in 2013
🎨 Graphics: ✅ Still decent
⏱️ Length: ✅ 5.7 hours for my playthrough
📖 Story: ✅ Good enough and entertaining
🎮 Gameplay: ✅ Classic cinematic Call of Duty
🐛 Bugs: ✅ No major issues for me now

[h2]What I liked[/h2]

* I enjoyed the campaign again, even on my second playthrough.
* The game still delivers that classic cinematic Call of Duty feeling.
* The skyscraper mission with rappelling was one of the most memorable parts for me.
* The jungle mission also stood out.
* Honestly, all missions had something enjoyable in them.
* The main villain was pretty good and carried a lot of the story for me.
* The campaign is short, but well-paced.
* It is not the best Call of Duty, but I still think it belongs among the better ones.

[h2]About the story[/h2]
I know some players did not like the missions or the story, but we also have to be honest here.

After the original Modern Warfare trilogy and Black Ops 1 and 2, it was extremely difficult to bring another Call of Duty campaign with the same level of cinematic impact.

Ghosts does not reach those heights, but I still think it offers a solid military action campaign.

[h2]Nostalgic details[/h2]
One thing that made me smile was the sound design.

This game came out in 2013, exactly 10 years after the original Call of Duty from 2003. Because of that, it felt strangely nostalgic to hear some familiar sounds again.

The footsteps in snow, picking up ammo from weapons on the ground, and walking on metal stairs sounded almost exactly like in the 2003 game.

Maybe some people will not care about that, but for me it was a nice nostalgic detail.

[h2]What didn’t work for me[/h2]

* It does not reach the level of the original Modern Warfare trilogy or Black Ops 1 and 2.
* The story is good, but not legendary.
* Some players may find the campaign too short.
* I can understand why not everyone connected with this entry.
* It probably did not do enough to become the start of a successful Ghosts sub-series.

[h2]Is it an endless game? How long to beat?[/h2]
No, this is not an endless game.

I finished the campaign in 5.7 hours. It is a typical shorter Call of Duty campaign, focused on cinematic missions and fast pacing.

[h2]Who will love it[/h2]
You will probably enjoy Call of Duty: Ghosts if you like cinematic military shooters, classic Call of Duty campaigns, short action-packed stories, and older CoD games from the Xbox 360 / PS3 / early Xbox One era.

[h2]Replay value[/h2]
Replay value is decent if you like replaying Call of Duty campaigns.

For me, this was my second full playthrough, and I still enjoyed it. I do not think I will replay it often, but I am glad I returned to it.

[h2]Final note[/h2]
Call of Duty: Ghosts is not the best Call of Duty, but I think it is better than its reputation suggests.

The campaign is short, cinematic, enjoyable, and has some memorable missions. The villain worked well for me, and the game gave me a bit of nostalgia because of some classic Call of Duty sound effects.

After Modern Warfare and Black Ops, expectations were extremely high, and Ghosts probably could not fully live up to them.

But as a single-player campaign, I still had a good time.

Recommended to play at least once.

Well, here we are again: another year, another [i]Call of Duty[/i], as the saying goes.

This franchise has grown incredibly stale in the past five years or so. Infinity Ward has stuck to the same formula since [i]Call of Duty 4: Modern Warfare[/i], and as a result, almost everything in [i]Ghosts[/i] feels dated and unimaginative.

Not that some widely acclaimed aspects of said formula needed any change. For instance, the core gameplay mechanics, such as the [i]shooting[/i] itself, still feel slick and polished.

But how do you justify a 50-gigabyte installation size and the “next-gen” marketing this game received, when it looks barely nicer than stuff that was released in 2007? It’s not an ugly-looking game, sure, and the textures do look pretty good, despite what some people may say. But comparisons with [i]Battlefield 4[/i], [i]Metro: Last Light[/i] and other recent titles are inevitable, and the fact remains that everything else in [i]Ghosts[/i], graphics-wise (lighting, particle effects, physics, etc.), is subpar.

I am not one to judge a game solely on its graphical fidelity, however. The problem with [i]Ghosts[/i] is that, sans the welcome addition of the ability to practice against bots, it has no redeeming qualities to speak of.

The single-player campaign is short, cliché-ridden and does not give the player any freedom. You just follow scripted orders from your “A.I.” companions, moving forward when told to and shooting enemies that pop out of hiding (when told to). It doesn’t help that the story is entirely predictable and that the voice-acting is abysmal (and since we're on the subject of audio, what can I say about the game's single, useless "master volume" slider in the settings menu?).

But most people seem to buy [i]Call of Duty[/i] games for its multiplayer portion. And it too is a colossal failure. Maps are poorly designed and don’t support more than 18 players (most matches have 12 or less players). The matchmaking system is terrible: teams are completely unbalanced more often than not. There are no dedicated servers, despite Mark Rubin’s (Infinity Ward’s Executive Producer) promises prior to the game’s release. Teamwork is non-existent, as people just run in circles and shoot each other in the back to get the best possible kill-to-death ratio and unlock ridiculous, balance-breaking “killstreak” bonuses.

Then there is the fact that once again, Activision will charge a good deal of money for upcoming map-packs, since not only is modding unsupported, but frowned upon.

The "new" Extinction Mode is not even worth discussing. It is basically an uninspired rehash of Treyarch's far superior "Zombies" horde-mode (from [i]World at War[/i] and the [i]Black Ops[/i] series).

To top it all, [i]Ghosts[/i] suffers from a myriad of technical issues, such as glitches, crashes and framerate drops. And as a sign of Infinity Ward's everlasting "love" for the PC audience, there is no field-of-view slider of any kind, and a single slider for audio. Individual sliders for music, sound effects and voice communication would be too much to ask, apparently.

The bottom line: don’t buy it.

UPDATE (07/31/2014): I should add that, at this point (almost a year after release), the game has become nothing but a glorified DLC-selling platform, and there's effectively nothing to differentiate it from the dozens of low-quality free-to-play games on the market... except for, you know, the full entry price.

Call of Duty: Ghosts was my first Call of Duty, so I’ve got a lot of nostalgia attached to it. I remember really enjoying the campaign back in the day, and the multiplayer felt solid enough at the time for me to sink a lot of hours into it.

Coming back years later, though, it’s pretty clear where the problems are. The multiplayer is basically dead most of the time, and when you do find lobbies, the gameplay tends to slow down a lot because of camping. Maps don’t really help either — a lot of them encourage that kind of passive play, which kills the flow of matches.

The campaign still holds up decently if you’re just looking for a one-time playthrough, but outside of that, there’s not much left here in terms of long-term value. It feels very much like a product of its time, and not one that aged particularly well compared to other entries in the series.

If you’re buying this today hoping for an active multiplayer experience, you’ll probably be disappointed. If it’s for nostalgia or to replay the campaign, then it can still be worth a look. Otherwise, there are better and more active Call of Duty titles out there, like Call of Duty: Black Ops II.

I bought this game on sale mainly because I was attracted by the reveal trailer and the 'dog' tag, and I am glad that I made this choice. The product I am reviewing is the singleplayer part of the game, as the multiplayer version is separate from the campaign on Steam and I never downloaded it. However, I know that this game is regarded as one of, if not THE, worst COD of all time for its multiplayer, and I can kind of see why that might be the case. Indeed, the gameplay is far from the best I experienced in a COD game, with gunplay being extremely average and movement feeling a bit odd at times. Although these features make the game slightly less enjoyable to play, they certainly do not destroy the singleplayer experience, as they are barely noticeable when you get used to them.

This brings me to the most important aspect of the review, which is the campaign itself. I can confidently say that this game features an amazing campaign, probably one of the best in the genre from many points of view. First of all, the setting is different from the usual WW2, Cold War or modern days settings that we are so used to seeing in COD games, with its futuristic, almost post-apocalyctic America already making the campaign intriguing and unique.
What the game does best from the beginning of the story is giving players the feeling of always being outnumbered and insignificant against the massive enemy 'Federation', making every mission seem almost impossible, which gives you an extra amount of motivation and an immense feeling of reward and satisfaction after a success, as well as immersing players even more into the story.
Everything is executed really well by the developers, with a gripping premise to the story, a likeable protagonist and an exceptionally well-written, chilling villain. Also the structure of the campaign is very enjoyable, with always interesting missions with varied settings and gameplay mechanics, some of which I still remember in detail for just how good and memorable they were. Especially the stealth or infiltration-type missions really stuck with me as they perfectly incorporated the feeling from the previous paragraph and the 'ghosts' vibe. Also, the dog gameplay was extremely fun and Riley is certainly the most adorable character in the game and, in my opinion, in the whole franchise.

Overall, I must say that there are so many wonderful aspects in this campaign that make the game so enjoyable and massively outweigh its issues. Indeed, the story is lovely from beginning to end (with an amazing ending sequence and a big plot-twist at the very end), the gameplay issues are almost unnoticeable in the campaign and overshadowed by some insane missions (although they do become slightly more relevant on Veteran difficulty, which was certainly not as nice of an experience as in other COD games), characters and settings are spot-on and graphics are not at all bad considering how old the game is. Don't listen to the critiques and buy it if it's on sale!

Okay, I'm preparing my self for this being a very unpopular review; but here goes.  Please also bare in mind that this review is purely and solely based on the single player side of the game - I will touch on the multiplayer side but only briefly. 

Call of Duty: Ghost is the tenth game in the COD series, and was released in 2013 on PC, PS3, Xbox 360 and Wii U, and then re-released on launch of PS4 and Xbox One. 

This was my first COD game that I had played in a while, so the problems people have had with the gameplay becoming stale and lack of innovation didn't effect me so much. Yes the gameplay is very much the same as all of the other Call of Duty games, however I still had fun whilst playing it. I have yet to play the multiplayer, and to be honest, I probably won't. The single player campaign follows the character of Logan Walker. You also play as Baker, Elias Walker (your father) and a new addition of playing as a combat dog, Riley.  There are no new elements to be seen in the gameplay, its very "Call of Duty", aim and shoot is pretty much the whole game with the odd quick time event thrown in. There are some really interesting levels when you are in space and underwater, however my favorite levels were the vehicle based ones; where you take control over tanks and helicopters - they add a little something extra to the game in my opinion, breaking up the monotony of the classic ground troop fights. 

Graphically, Ghosts is very dated; I was playing on 4K resolution, and it still looked very poor. Textures when close up are so low res it's hard to imagine this is a game which was released in 2013. The game uses an engine which was used in previous COD releases, but with apparent "significant upgrades", however I don't really see a difference in graphic fidelity in Ghosts and any of the other "recent" COD games. 

Ghost had a story which kept me interested right until the end, however I felt that the game's ending really did not do the game any justice. I really felt like I was getting a big two fingers up to me when it happened. Not sure whether people will class it as a spoiler, but the cliffhanger at the end really relies on there being a sequel in the Ghost franchise, however unlikely that will be. Up until the end though, it is a compelling story - maybe if you quit just before the end credits you'll enjoy it more! 

This is another game where you will not die or fail on the single player mode; you are with a squad of other characters for the majority of the game; and you could very easily just sit back and watch the fire fights if you were so inclined and you would still not fail. Even when playing on higher difficulties, there is no real ramp in the challenges on show. 

With the games extremely linear level design, it leaves you very little time to explore the world in front of you, that being said, there is no reason to want to either though. There are one set of "collectibles" to be on the look out for, and that's it - I guess it is to be expected from a COD game though. It would of been nice to maybe find little bits of extra plot and story through hacking computers, finding files etc. 

The single player mode took me just about seven hours to finish - I thought that was an OK length for the game;  I wasn't growing tired of the gameplay by the end of the game but there is no reason at all to play it through for a second time - expect of course if you want to play on a higher difficulty; but even then, I wouldn't say it's worth it.  Where you are going to get your mileage out of any COD game is the multiplayer - however I still don't plan on playing it simply because I am not interested in the multiplayer side of many games. 

Technically I didn't have any bugs or issues whilst playing. I was able to play on a steady 60 fps on 4k resolution the whole play through. At times the frame rate was even in the 100s. It certainly looks like the PC version of the game came out on top of the consoles on the technical side of things, since the consoles could barely even achieve 60 fps on lower resolutions, Xbox could only handle 720p. This game is better off being played with a keyboard and mouse, however the lack of FOV sliders did make me feel a little bit nauseous with the camera swaying around all of the time when moving. You can change this in .ini settings but in this day in age, PC games need a FOV slider as compulsory in my opinion. 

In conclusion, whilst there may seem to be more negatives than positives in my review for Ghosts, I did have a lot of fun whilst playing it, however the price of £39,99 is absolutely ridiculously especially for a game which has been out almost two years now.  If like me you are just going to play the single player mode, wait for the game to be around £10, but if you are going to be jumping into the multiplayer side of things (there is still a very active community out there too!) I would happily say you can pick this up for anything below £15 - since you will get the seven hour single player as well as many many hours of CODs core element, multiplayer.

Call of Duty: Ghosts has really good visuals in my opinion. Textures and effects are pretty nice, lightning is all right too, but at certain places, it's pretty overly exaggerated. There are not many elements on the HUD, which I found it all right and clean. It's not distracting and fits this alternative future scenario. The story and the overall universe of this game is quite interesting. The first mission was astonishing to look at it and had some pretty cool vibes. About vibes, playing this game is bringing COD 2 and COD 4 feelings in me, it's pretty similar to those games in my opinion, which I like. Most of the characters have their own story, which was nice to see. The ending was quite surprising too, which brings up a few questions, but it was interesting to see something unusual. The gun play was unusual for me at first. Most weapons have some insane recoil, but I think it makes the game more challenging, which is better.

I'm not saying this is a negative aspect, but after Black Ops 2, this game doesn't have multiple endings, or strike force missions or custom loadouts for campaign missions. It was a nice addition, but it's not that bad if they cut those out in this one.

However, what I didn't liked, it's the beginning of the game. After the first mission, the next several one was really boring for me. There were not many actions, it's mostly showing the situation in the world and introducing characters, which I understand it's not that exciting, but it was still really tiring to get through. Same goes to the story: after the first mission, it gets a bit confusing about why are we going and where, whats our goal and why certain characters are in that location. I didn't understood it well. The peaking system is different in this game: now you can't peak with buttons, but if you behind a cover and an arrow shows up next to your crosshair, indication where you will peak when you aim... and honestly, I was never able to utilize this completely and it was annoying to get into position and use it, quite a trash system. Even though I said the HUD is all right, which is, but the weapon placement on my screen is not. It takes so much space on my screen, it's criminal. There are many parts, where the game is quite dark and enemies are hard to see in general.

I wasn't sure if I'm going to like this COD game first, but honestly it's not bad. Maybe it's the weakest COD games which came out before this, but it was solid and likable, after the campaign picked up the pace. I can recommend it to buy this game, but not for 60€, 20€ is fine for it. Do not buy the DLCs if you aim to play it in multiplayer. Get the Plutonium launcher and get the additonal DLCs from there.

[b]Call of Duty: Ghosts[/b]

I believe most people's opinion of this title is clouded with the circumstance of its release, being right after one of the best in the franchise and not satisfying any new itch. In the same vein, my opinion is likely equally clouded with nostalgia. Being the first in the franchise I owned myself, replaying it again as an adult only further solidified for me that this game doesn't deserve the hate. If you compare it to the previous Infinity Ward titles, it is very similar, and with the following releases, much better. It is almost dead now but worth mentioning, the multiplayer was very average, more reaction oriented with a fast time to kill. Since they're so similar, it was more bland than Modern Warfare 2, but it was more fair with more content. There are a share of dull moments but overall, every mission in the campaign has you doing badass special ops sh*t and the whole plot goes hard all the way through. Being more modern of a title with better graphics, sounds and voices, it sells everything better than its Modern Warfare predecessors, but still has the solid story elements unlike the following titles. For me I think the developers made a goldilocks story, they made a great antagonist, made it personal, made a squad and cause you care about, made some solid unique settings then delivered. What especially does it for me is the scenes climbing around a skyscraper at night for intel, sneaking around the rain forest enemies everywhere, fighting in space on a suicide mission and of course the credits. Sounds so clique and corny, yes, but are we so critical and hard-assed that we can't pretend to play super soldier for a few hours? No one argues this game to be a list topper, but it is far from the game that ruined the franchise.
